 One Possession: C's rookie validates high praise from Jayson Tatum 
 Chris Cenac Jr. is making the most of his minutes. 
 By Chris Forsberg, Celtics Insider • 
 Published November 17, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 17, 2026 at 6:44 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Chris Forsberg and Eddie House join Kayla Burton to offer instant reaction and analysis following the Boston Celtics’ 115-105 loss to the Orlando Magic. Boston, playing on the second night of a back-to-backs, kept the game close, but Orlando outscored the C’s 40-28 to snap their six-game win streak and drop the green to 11-3 on the season.
 Boston Celtics rookie Chris Cenac Jr. had already received the Jayson Tatum stamp of approval 24 hours earlier, but, as if to confirm the praise administered by his All-Star teammate, Cenac Jr. delivered a pair of loud alley-oop dunks during Monday’s tilt with the Orlando Magic.
 Thrust into the most robust minutes of his young NBA career as the Celtics rested veteran big man Neemias Queta, the 19-year-old Cenac Jr. chipped in four points and two rebounds over a career-high 12 minutes of game action. He even made a crunch-time cameo.

 His two alley-oop finishes helped Boston pull ahead of Orlando late in the third quarter. That was balanced out by two turnovers on consecutive possessions later in the frame. But Cenac Jr. has made quite an impression in a short time in green.
 "Chris gonna be good,” Tatum told reporters after Boston’s win over Dallas on Sunday night. "Chris is good now. But he's really, really gonna be good.”
 View this post on Instagram 
 Cenac Jr., the 27th pick in June’s draft, wasn’t expected to see much court time with Boston given a well-stocked big-man depth chart featuring Queta, Mitchell Robinson, and Luka Garza. But a big early lead against Dallas, and Queta’s day off against Orlando, opened the door to some extended run for Cenac Jr., who won’t stop throwing down alley-oop lobs.
 In fact, seven of his 12 attempts, and all seven of his makes this season, have been dunks.
 For a Celtics team that has struggled to connect with newcomer Robinson on lobs, Cenac Jr. has made it look rather easy. He tends to float around the basket, and teammates have rewarded him for strong cuts.
 The Celtics have only scratched the surface with Cenac Jr., whose springy ways should make him an excellent shot blocker and contester at the NBA level. Boston has him working extensively on his perimeter shot with hopes of stretching out his range early in his NBA career.

 Cenac Jr. should spend much of his winter getting reps with the Maine Celtics. He’s averaging 13.7 points, 9.3 rebounds, 1.7 blocks, and 1.7 assists in three G League appearances. He won’t turn 20 until Feb. 1. Cenac Jr. was four months old when teammate Mike Conley was drafted in June of 2007.
 The Celtics have had good luck with big men drafted out of the state of Louisiana. Bill Russell (Monroe, La.) won 11 NBA titles, while Robert Parish (Shreveport, La.) won three more. Glen Davis (Baton Rouge) won a title with Boston in 2008, while Robert Williams III (Vivian, La.) shined as a lob threat earlier this decade. Robinson also has Louisiana roots after attending Chalmette High School.
